scope: First 40 of the 164-paper screening-delta queue, coded highest-citation first.
criteria: RQ3: does the paper propose a NAMED distinct attack technique or degradation mechanism? RQ4: does it propose a NAMED distinct defense? Surveys, taxonomies, evaluation-only and dataset-only papers contribute neither.

coded.title: Not What You've Signed Up For

rq3.name: Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI)
rq3.note: ORIGIN paper for IPI - the registry already has the entry, extracted from a later paper. This should become its source. Also names prompt worming (self-propagating IPI) and information-ecosystem contamination as sub-classes.

rq4.name: Instruction Hierarchy (privileged-instruction training)
rq4.note: Model-level training so the LLM ranks system prompts above untrusted text. Cited as a baseline across the corpus.

rq3.name: Combined Attack (Open-Prompt-Injection)
rq3.note: Formalizes 5 techniques - Naive, Escape Characters, Context Ignoring, Fake Completion, Combined - and proposes Combined as new. This is the OpenPromptInjection harness DataSentinel and our own RQ6 reconstruction run on; it was flagged as out-of-corpus in benchmark_mechanism_inventory.json and is now in.

rq4.name: StruQ (structured queries)
rq4.note: Secure front-end separating prompt and data channels plus a structured instruction-tuned LLM. Named by 7 uncovered mechanisms' papers as the defense they tested against.

rq3.name: BIPIA benchmark attack set
rq3.note: Benchmark-contributed, same category as AgentDojo/InjecAgent/ASB. 14 defenses in the corpus evaluate on it.

rq4.name: Boundary awareness + explicit reminder
rq4.note: Two defenses: black-box (explicit reminder) and white-box (boundary awareness).

rq4.name: Spotlighting (delimiting / datamarking / encoding)
rq4.note: The provenance-signalling family everyone benchmarks against; named by 9 uncovered mechanisms' papers.

rq3.name: Virtual Prompt Injection (VPI)
rq3.note: FLAG FOR REVIEW. The backdoor is installed by poisoning instruction-tuning data, which the screening criteria exclude as training-time-only. It manifests at runtime with no input injection, so it is genuinely borderline. Recommend excluding to stay consistent with the stated criteria, and recording the call.

rq3.name: JudgeDeceiver
rq3.note: Gradient-optimised injection against LLM-as-a-Judge selection.

rq4.name: SecAlign (preference optimization)
rq4.note: The ORIGINAL SecAlign. The corpus already has 'Meta SecAlign', its successor; these are distinct entries. Named by 7 uncovered mechanisms' papers.

rq3.name: UNNAMED: automatic universal gradient-based prompt injection
rq3.note: Momentum-enhanced gradient method producing universal injection strings; no product name given.

rq3.name: Tensor Trust: prompt extraction / prompt hijacking
rq3.note: Benchmark-contributed. Names two attack classes and supplies 126k human-generated attacks.

rq4.note: 46k prompt-based 'defenses' are dataset entries, not a proposed defense.

rq3.name: distraction effect (attention shift to injected instruction)
rq3.note: A mechanistic explanation rather than an attack technique; recorded as an ML/AI-style mechanism.

rq4.name: Attention Tracker
rq4.note: Training-free detection from attention patterns on the instruction. Named by uncovered mechanisms' papers as a baseline.

coded.title: From Prompt Injections to SQL Injection

rq3.name: P2SQL injection (prompt-to-SQL)
rq3.note: Prompt injection chained into SQL injection through LangChain middleware.

rq4.name: UNNAMED: P2SQL mitigations (DB permission hardening + query rewriting)

rq3.name: CyberSecEval 2: prompt-injection + code-interpreter-abuse test set
rq3.note: Benchmark-contributed and broad; low confidence that it is a distinct mechanism rather than an evaluation suite.

coded.title: Assessing PI Risks in 200+ Custom GPTs

rq3.name: UNNAMED: system-prompt and uploaded-file extraction from custom GPTs

rq4.name: f-secure LLM system (information flow control)
rq4.note: Already cited BY defenses in the corpus (PACT and NeuroTaint both baseline against 'f-secure'/FIDES). Its own paper was outside the corpus until now.

rq3.name: UNNAMED: adaptive attack suite bypassing 12 PI/jailbreak defenses
rq3.note: HIGH VALUE for the reverse scan - it runs 12 defenses and bypasses most above 90% ASR, against defenses that reported near-zero. Should be re-scanned for (defense, mechanism) pairs once ingested.

rq3.name: HackAPrompt: prompt-hacking taxonomy and 600k-prompt corpus
rq3.note: Competition dataset plus taxonomy; borderline as a distinct mechanism.

rq4.name: Signed-Prompt
rq4.note: Authorised users sign sensitive instructions so the LLM can tell trusted instruction sources apart.

rq3.note: Benchmark and measurement only; proposes no new technique.

coded.title: Demystifying RCE Vulnerabilities in LLM-Integrated Apps

rq3.name: LLMSmith: prompt-injection-to-RCE exploitation
rq3.note: Static call-chain analysis plus prompt-based exploitation reaching remote code execution through LangChain-style utilities.

coded.title: Can Indirect PI Attacks Be Detected and Removed?

rq4.name: UNNAMED: IPI detection + post-detection removal pipeline
rq4.note: Also contributes a detection/removal benchmark. Directly relevant to the sanitizer family.

rq4.name: PromptShield (fine-tuned deployable PI detector)
rq4.note: Detector plus a curation benchmark; targets the low-false-positive regime.

coded.title: An Early Categorization of Prompt Injection Attacks
Adversarial Attacks of Vision Tasks: A Survey

rq4.name: PIGuard (Mitigating Over-defense for Free)
rq4.note: NOTE: distinct from IPIGuard, which is already in the registry - an earlier probe of mine conflated them. Contributes the NotInject over-defense dataset.

rq4.name: InjecGuard
rq4.note: FLAG: near-identical abstract to PIGuard above, same NotInject dataset and same MOF training strategy, differing only in the reported margin (30.8% vs 30.4%). Almost certainly the same work under two titles - a rename across versions. Treat as ONE defense and retract the duplicate; do not count both.

coded.title: Red Teaming the Mind of the Machine

rq4.name: DefensiveToken (test-time optimized special tokens)
rq4.note: Test-time defense with training-time-comparable robustness; already cited as a baseline inside the corpus.

rq3.name: G2PIA (goal-guided generative prompt injection)
rq3.note: Black-box attack maximising KL divergence between clean and adversarial conditionals.

rq3.name: knowledge conflict (contextual vs parametric)
rq3.note: Track B. The registry already has related knowledge-conflict entries; check for overlap before adding.

coded.title: A Critical Evaluation of Defenses against PI

rq3.name: UNNAMED: adaptive prompt-injection attacks for defense evaluation (PIEval)
rq3.note: HIGH VALUE for the reverse scan - shows existing defenses are less successful than reported, across two dimensions. Re-scan once ingested.

coded.title: Ranking Manipulation for Conversational Search Engines

rq3.name: UNNAMED: tree-of-attacks ranking manipulation for conversational search
rq3.note: Injection that promotes low-ranked products in an LLM search engine's citation order; transfers across models.

coded.title: PI Against LLM-Integrated Mobile Robotic Systems

rq3.name: UNNAMED: multi-modal prompt injection against robot navigation

rq4.name: UNNAMED: secure prompt strategies for robotic navigation
PromptLocate (injected-prompt localization)
rq4.note: Already cited as a baseline inside the corpus (the Relinking paper's source-sanitizer group). Its own paper was outside the corpus until now.

rq3.name: preemptive answer attack (CoT short-circuiting)
rq3.note: The LLM obtains an answer before reasoning, degrading CoT. Cross-track flavour: arises inadvertently OR by injection.

rq3.name: EchoLeak (zero-click IPI, CVE-2025-32711)
rq3.note: Real production exploit in M365 Copilot chaining XPIA-classifier evasion, link-redaction bypass, auto-fetched images and a Teams proxy. A rare in-the-wild case.

rq4.note: Proposes engineering mitigations but no named, evaluated defense.

rq3.note: Uses IPI as a benign watermarking TOOL, not as an attack studied. Out of scope.
